utterances.text: I know it will be corrected later on, it's monetary not monastery system as it's -- as the record reflects. If we go on to the next document, 1D 02226. This is dated 25 January 1991. 1D 02226. Here it's from Oslobodjenje, this is a, as we know, a publication from Sarajevo and it would appear that, based on this article, we see that the government or the executive council, the assembly of SRBH, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted a bill that would authorise the republic government to clear debts with the federation without its agreement. Then further in the next paragraph, it says, "The government would temporarily prohibit the execution of the federal finance secretary's order for the transfer of funds from the republic budget account for the repayment of international credits for which the federation provided guarantees or super-guarantees." I don't want to -- the very last paragraph on the page also -- and going on to the second page says, "Last year, the particular problem was that the federation was late in meeting all of its obligations towards BH and especially its obligation arising from foreign credit -- credits, payments of differences in exchange rates, pensions and disability benefits, and obligations arising from the system -- from the citizens' foreign currency savings and social programmes," and here we have the figure of 11.14 billion dinar obligation. The federation paid 4.81 billion. Now based on this, can we conclude -- what can we conclude about the Bosnian economy at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: The interpretation was not right. I did not fully follow your speech. If we are not going to repeat this while I did understand the question I can give my comments with regard to this text if allowed to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, if you could be brief.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: This has to do with a proposal of a decision of the executive council, that is to say, the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And it is my understanding that the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina would say supposed to approve the text. That is what it says in the first part of the text. I do not know whether the assembly did indeed approve this kind of proposal made by the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, however, I would like to remind you of what I said a few moments ago. The incursion into the monetary system of Yugoslavia meant the beginning of the disintegration of that system. Probably all governments in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in all the other republics were trying to defend themselves and protect themselves. I assume, I assume that this is part of the policy that the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina tried to adopt when the monetary system of the country as a whole was disintegrating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes that section. I just wanted to give the Trial Chamber a sense of what the times were like prior to the relevant events that concern us. Now, if we go to the next document which is 1D 02687, 2687. I know there's going to be a question from the Bench about the timing of this so I will be referring after this document to 1D 02688 which is 6 March 1992. And I'm saying that so that -- to alleviate any concerns from anyone in and around the Court. Now, we know from the first document that you were not yet the Minister of Finance at this point in time but would it be fair to say that from your involvement as minister and from your occupation as an economist, you would be able to provide us some insight as far as non-residential accounts and what this document purports to be?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: Two sentences by way of an introduction, if you allow me. All the economies of the republics, that is to say, of Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, up until 1990 were part of a unified economic system. From 1990 onwards, the states started becoming increasingly independent and every one of them started establishing its own economic system. It is understandable that at a moment when states started separating from Yugoslavia, there were many economic relations that remained unresolved. Many companies from Bosnia and Herzegovina had claims vis-a-vis Croatia, Serbia and vice versa. None of the new states had enough foreign currency to make the necessary payments. Life had to go on. Economic systems were supposed to continue functioning. The state systems found a solution through this system of non-residential accounts. I would like to look at the next document in article 3, it says that non-residential accounts will be used or rather the relations between and among republics will be resolved by way of payments of goods and services in the domestic currency or in foreign currency. Let me be practical. That meant that a company from Bosnia and Herzegovina that had outstanding claims from Croatia and that could not have the appropriate payments paid because Croatia did not have enough foreign currency opened a non-residential account in a Croatian bank and then the Croatian enterprise paid money into this account. In this way, the Bosnian company had Croatian dinars on an account in Croatia. In this way, this company could buy goods in Croatia and make payments from that account. Non-residential accounts, therefore, were accounts that made it possible to resolve the problem or, rather, bridge the gap as Yugoslavia was falling apart in order to have financial relations resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Two points. One, the document that you were referring to when you said Article 3, that was 1D 02688; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also we can see from this document that this payment agreement from the very -- from the preamble, we see that the two governments are involved, the government of the Republic of Croatia and the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: According to the agreement, that is correct. According to the document, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to have to ask you to slow down a little bit when you give an answer because they have to be translated and --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The interpreters work so hard and I'm going to be held responsible if I don't slow you down. We'll go to the next document, 1D 02686. 2686. This document, if we look at the second page at the bottom, we see your name, Dr. Zarko Primorac. It makes reference to the 6 March -- to that date that we previously saw. Can you tell us what this is? What this payment agreement reflects?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The government that I was not in, that is to say, that functioned before the government that I was elected to, had signed a payments agreement with the Republic of Croatia. That is the preceding document. The 6th of March, 1992. That is the heading. When I joined the government and became a minister, then we saw that some things in this agreement had to be changed. For example, just to draw your attention to a minor detail, in the preamble of the first document, the document dated the 6th of March, 1992, it is stated that the government of the Republic of Croatia at a meeting held on the 17th of February, 1992, and the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, signed, et cetera, et cetera. In the new agreement, we deleted the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina because it was no longer that. It was called the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As for the content of the agreement, appropriate provisions were taken over from the previous agreement and new provisions were also introduced that were topical at the time. The text of the agreement is one that I negotiated with the Republic of Croatia. On the Croatian side, it was Minister Jasic who was authorised to negotiate the text. We did indeed negotiate this and we brought matters to an end, rather, to the signing the agreement. You can see on the document that the Republic of Croatia signed the document. I did not sign the document because at that time, I did not have the consent of Sarajevo because the government probably had not discussed the matter and did not give me an appropriate signal to have this signed. Therefore, it remained unsigned on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you had anticipated before that we would be interested in the date of another document. This also has no date. Perhaps Dr. Primorac, perhaps you could indicate the date of this unsigned and, finally, not concluded draft agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This agreement on payments with Croatia that I had negotiated was negotiated in the second half of September 1992. Probably this was concluded towards the end of October 1992. The rule is or, rather, practice is to affix the date when the government approved the agreement. I don't see why there is no date next to Minister Jasic's signature, that is to say the minister of finance of the Republic of Croatia. I could not have such a date because quite simply, the government had not approved of that agreement in my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, 1D 0 -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Karnavas. It is only a technical matter. The witness said that according to the practice, the agreements are being referred to according to the date when the government approves them or accepts them. According to my knowledge and experience, it is in a way not correct. Usually, the concluded agreements are being given the date when they are signed by those who are negotiating it and to work them out and, of course, the approval or certification is another cup of tea and it was -- it is -- it should be then later on mentioned but anyway, I -- agreement or treaty should be referred to according to the first acceptance of it by the parties concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you take any exception -- did you want to comment on that, His Honour's observations?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: I acknowledge this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. 1D 02689. 2689. This is dated 31 December 1991. It's an agreement, if we look at the preamble, we see that it's the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Croatia and the Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now, this is 31 December 1991. We probably should have dealt with this a little earlier. We see that in Article 2, it says, "In order to conduct payment transactions from Article 1 of this agreement, participants in the payment transaction based in the Republic of Croatia may open separate accounts with the public auditing service of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the domestic currency which is current in the territory of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Could you please explain what that means and why it would have been necessary for this agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: Please give me a minute to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Karnavas, are you sure that 31 December is the date of this agreement? It seems to me that there are signatures with dates in March and the 31st December is a date from which certain effects should be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. I stand corrected and maybe because I -- I'm a little tired, but -- even though we're not that much into the day, I see that there is an agreement on the manner of conducting payment transactions and that's dated 31 December. And now, because I'm wondering how could I have made such a mistake to, now I see that it's 19th of March, 1992, that it's signed on one side, and it looks like it's February 1992, on the other by Jozo Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you can't help us we'll move on to the next document?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO PRIMORAC
utterances.text: That's impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those after us cannot wait. We have to stop here for today. You will continue tomorrow, Witness. The hearing starts at 9.00. That's when we will resume. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
